<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD fetches the gVisor source code from its official GitHub repository (https://github.com/google/gvisor) using a tagged release, which aligns with standard and secure packaging practices. The checksum for the source tarball is provided and matches the expected SHA-256 hash, ensuring source integrity. A local patch (`crosstool-archlinux.patch`) is applied during prepare(), which is common for adapting build systems to Arch Linux tooling, and a simple version script is generated—both are benign and transparent operations.

The build process uses `bazel-real` (presumably a system-installed Bazel) to compile two components: `runsc` and the `containerd-shim-runsc-v1`. The use of `--repository_cache` and `--output_user_root` helps ensure reproducibility and avoids network access during build, while `--nofetch` in the build() phase further prevents remote downloads at that stage. The `prepare()` phase does perform a `fetch`, but it is limited to the declared targets and uses the same flags, reducing the risk of unauthorized network activity. No obfuscated code, suspicious downloads, or data exfiltration mechanisms are present.

The package installs only the compiled binaries into standard system paths and declares appropriate dependencies, conflicts, and provides. All operations are consistent with standard AUR packaging practices for a Bazel-based project. There are no signs of malicious behavior such as unauthorized network requests, execution of external scripts, or system tampering.
</details>
